Padding/masking/expansion mechanisms themselves are independently verified correct (14/14 unit tests). Informs exp0002 (frozen-backbone warm-up) directly.

interpretation: Refutes the leading hypothesis: with the entire backbone provably frozen/unchanged, LIBERO-Spatial got WORSE (73.33%->16.67%) not better. Re-diagnosis: action_encoder/head are shared weight matrices whose column/row ranges overlap between LIBERO (0-6) and RoboTwin (0-13) -- RoboTwin's gradient directly updates the same columns LIBERO depends on, and with the backbone frozen there is no downstream plasticity to compensate. Points to per-embodiment-separated projection weights (not a shared K=14 projection) as the next fix.
modifications: Added Trainer.trainable_modules=expanded_projections_only: freeze entire shared MoT backbone, train only action_encoder/head/proprio_encoder (6 tensors)
Otherwise identical to exp0001: K=14 padding, masked loss, embodiment-conditioned prompts, ~1:1 interleaving, 1000 steps, LR 3e-5
what_to_watch: Whether LIBERO retention improves vs exp0001; whether RoboTwin still shows zero learning with fewer trainable params.
why_this_might_help: Investigation of exp0001 hypothesized the unmasked video loss trains the shared backbone on RoboTwin's different visual domain, hurting LIBERO; freezing the backbone should isolate/prevent this.

interpretation: Result contradicts the simple disjoint-offset-fixes-it hypothesis: with the same trainable-backbone treatment as exp0001, disjoint projection offsets should have produced retention >= exp0001's 73.33% if projection-column overlap were the sole interference mechanism. Instead it landed at 50.00%, worse than exp0001, better than exp0002. Per-task pattern is scattered/task-swapping rather than a uniform decline (3 tasks fine in exp0001 dropped to 0%, 3 different tasks weak in exp0001 hit 100%), consistent with either meaningful run-to-run variance on a small 3-trial/task panel or a new instability source from RoboTwin's all-fresh-init projection weights (vs exp0001's partial warm-start via reused/corrupted LIBERO weights). Combined with exp0002 (backbone freezing alone also failed), points toward the shared transformer backbone as an under-isolated interference channel -- no candidate so far has combined disjoint projections with a frozen backbone to test this cleanly. Recommends investigate-fastwam-problem before the next candidate.

what_to_watch: Whether LIBERO-Spatial sentinel retention recovers toward the 96.67% fresh-machine baseline, confirming the disjoint-offset fix eliminates the exp0001/exp0002 shared-weight-column interference; any RoboTwin learning signal.
why_this_might_help: Directly targets the re-diagnosed root cause of exp0001/exp0002's LIBERO regression: RoboTwin's real (non-padded) forward values previously overlapped LIBERO's valid weight columns because both embodiments were left-aligned at column 0 in the shared action_encoder/head/proprio_encoder. A disjoint per-embodiment offset makes this provably interference-free (see gradient-isolation unit test) without the much larger implementation risk of fully separate per-embodiment weight matrices.

interpretation: Completes the 2x2 matrix: overlap+trainable=73.33% (exp0001), overlap+frozen=16.67% (exp0002), disjoint+trainable=50.00% (exp0003), disjoint+frozen=63.33% (exp0004). Freezing the backbone has OPPOSITE effects depending on projection design: hurts with overlapping projections (73.33%->16.67%, no plasticity to compensate for projection corruption) but helps with disjoint projections (50.00%->63.33%, once projection corruption is eliminated, backbone drift becomes the dominant remaining interference channel and freezing removes it too). Confirms disjoint offsets are a real, substantial fix (huge 17%->63% jump isolated in the frozen-backbone regime) and that backbone-level drift is a second, independent interference channel. Still below exp0001's 73.33% and the 90% floor -- exp0001 (imperfect on both projection overlap AND full backbone plasticity) remains the best multi-embodiment retention result, suggesting backbone plasticity may provide some net-positive adaptation benefit that a full freeze forfeits, not yet isolated. task4 (bowl in top drawer) is 0% across every multi-embodiment candidate -- a persistently hard task independent of these design choices. RoboTwin progress check: click_alarmclock 33.3%/33.3% (clean/random) -- the first non-zero RoboTwin result anywhere in this project (exp0001 measured 0.0% everywhere including this exact task); adjust_bottle remained 0.0%/0.0%. Shows the frozen-backbone disjoint-offset recipe can produce real RoboTwin capability, not just avoid forgetting. Recommends exp0005 combine disjoint-offset projections with partial backbone plasticity (e.g. differential LR: much lower for backbone than projections) rather than a full freeze or full train.
modifications: Combined exp0002's backbone freezing (trainable_modules=expanded_projections_only) with exp0003's disjoint-offset projections (K=21/22, LIBERO offset 0, RoboTwin offset 7/8) -- the missing cell in the 2x2 backbone(trainable/frozen) x projections(overlapping/disjoint) design
No code changes -- Trainer._apply_expanded_projections_only_train_mode verified width-agnostic by reading it; reused exp0003's expanded checkpoint and data/config machinery unchanged
what_to_watch: Whether LIBERO-Spatial clears meaningfully above exp0002's 16.67% floor (tests whether disjoint offsets help once isolated from backbone-plasticity confound) and how it compares to exp0003's 50.00%.
why_this_might_help: exp0002 (frozen backbone, overlapping projections) and exp0003 (trainable backbone, disjoint projections) each confounded the variable they tested with the other axis. This candidate isolates disjoint-offset projections from backbone plasticity to determine whether backbone-level drift, not projection overlap, is the dominant interference mechanism.

interpretation: LIBERO-Spatial 63.33%, exactly matching exp0004 aggregate (different per-task mix, consistent with real per-task noise). RoboTwin progress check contradicts the candidate hypothesis: adjust_bottle stayed 0%/0% (unchanged), and click_alarmclock LOST its randomized-phase capability entirely (33.3%->0.0%), keeping only clean-phase result. Partial backbone plasticity did not unlock more RoboTwin learning -- it cost robustness under domain randomization for no gain. Two open questions before exp0006: (1) is exp0004's 33.3%/33.3% itself just n=3-episode noise, not a real capability exp0005 lost? (2) if real, does the 1000-step budget give the backbone too little RoboTwin-specific gradient signal to build something more robust than the frozen exp0019 representations already provided, i.e. is training budget the more relevant lever than the LR-ratio dial? Recommends -fastwam-problem before exp0006.

interpretation: LIBERO-Spatial 63.33%, exactly matching exp0004 and exp0005 despite 4x more training steps -- three candidates now converge on this ceiling regardless of training treatment. RoboTwin progress check: click_alarmclock LOST its only real capability entirely (33.3%/33.3% at step 1000 -> 0.0%/0.0% at step 4000, confirmed via raw result files), adjust_bottle stayed dead. Combined with exp0005 (different LR also regressed click_alarmclock), this shows exp0004's checkpoint sits near a narrow, fragile optimum for click_alarmclock specifically -- neither more steps nor a different backbone LR improves on it, both actively destroy it. Recommends investigate-fastwam-problem to check whether exp0004's result even reliably replicates (re-train fresh + re-evaluate with a different seed) before assuming it was a real, buildable capability rather than a lucky single measurement, prior to choosing exp0007.

interpretation: LIBERO-Spatial 56.67%, close to but not exactly the 63.33% seen in exp0004/0005/0006 -- confirms real (if narrow) run-to-run variance despite a near-identical training loss. RoboTwin (enlarged n=10 panel): click_alarmclock 20.0% clean / 10.0% random, confirmed via raw result files -- SETTLES the reproducibility question: exp0004's capability was real, not a lucky n=3 measurement, since a true-0% model cannot produce real physically-verified successes across independent seeds. The exact rate (~10-30%) is noisier and somewhat lower than exp0004's single-draw 33.3%/33.3%. adjust_bottle remains a clean 0% across 4 candidates now (12 real episodes, zero successes). Reframes exp0005/exp0006's apparent 0% regressions as ambiguous -- could be genuine destruction or just unlucky n=3 draws from a genuinely noisy modest true rate. Dominant unresolved problem remains LIBERO retention (56-63% band across 4 runs, all far below 90% floor; exp0001's 73.33% with OVERLAPPING projections + trainable backbone remains the single best retention result). Recommends exp0008 combine the interference-free disjoint-offset projections with a LIBERO-favoring data-mixing ratio (untested variable) on a trainable backbone.
